findings.title: Data races on shared err and counter in concurrent init
findings.body: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go init() launches one errgroup goroutine per namespace stat. Each goroutine does totalBatchesIndexed++ and _, _, err = s.build(...) where err is the outer variable from stats, err := GetResourceStats and totalBatchesIndexed is a plain int shared by all workers. With initWorkers > 1 this is concurrent unsynchronized read-modify-write on the same variables while the parent is blocked in group.Wait() and then reassigns err. This is a data race that corrupts the count, loses build errors, and trips the race detector.

findings.title: Removing BuildIndex lock allows duplicate builds for same key
findings.body: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go BuildIndex() previously held cacheMu for the whole build and now only locks around b.cache[key] = idx. GetIndex() only takes RLock and returns nil while a build is in flight, so concurrent init workers or concurrent Search-triggered getOrCreateIndex() for the same NamespacedResource will both run bleve.New(), both run the ListIterator builder, both increment IndexTenants, and both write the same file directory for file-backed indexes. The loser is leaked without Close and bleve file creation on the same path can fail with index-exists/lock errors. A coarse lock was slow but correct; the fix needs per-key singleflight, not no lock.

findings.title: TotalDocs reads cache map without lock
findings.body: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go TotalDocs() iterates for _, v := range b.cache with no cacheMu held while BuildIndex() concurrently does b.cache[key] = idx under Lock. In Go concurrent map read and write is a fatal runtime panic, not just a race. With builds now parallelized the window is large, and any concurrent metrics/logging call to TotalDocs during a lazy getOrCreateIndex build can crash the storage server.

findings.title: Watch goroutine never exits and panics on closed channel
findings.body: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go init() starts watchctx := context.Background() and go func() { for { v := <-events; s.handleEvent(watchctx, v) } } with no ok check and no Done handling. The sql backend poller does defer close(stream) on shutdown. After close, receive returns nil forever in a hot loop and handleEvent dereferences evt.Type on nil, causing nil panic and CPU spin. The goroutine also uses a Background context that is never cancelled on server Stop, so it leaks even on clean shutdown. It must watch server context Done and break on !ok.

findings.title: History/Origin panic when search not configured
findings.body: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go Search() checks if s.search == nil and returns an error, but History() and Origin() unconditionally do s.search.History/Origin. When SearchOptions.Resources is nil, newSearchSupport is skipped and s.search stays nil, which is a valid configuration. Any gRPC History or Origin call then nil-pointer panics and crashes the server instead of returning search-not-configured.

findings.title: Synchronous full reindex in constructor blocks startup
findings.body: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go NewResourceServer() now calls s.Init(ctx) synchronously, where ctx is the server-lifetime Background context. Init builds every search index via ListIterator over all namespaces before returning. Construction therefore blocks from milliseconds to minutes with no timeout and no way for the caller to cancel, delaying module readiness/health and making any index failure fatal to server creation. Previously reads/writes blocked only on first use; now nothing can start serving until all indexes finish.

findings.title: Skipping postgres storage-server test hides init regression
findings.body: In pkg/server/module_server_test.go the change adds a skip for postgres for TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer. This test exercises storage-server startup, which is exactly what the PR changes from lazy to eager init with DB-dependent GetResourceStats/ListIterator/watch polling. Skipping it means the new startup path is never validated on postgres in CI, so postgres-specific init hangs or failures will not be caught.
